plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling fields of slender silver-green stems topped with fragrant violet-blue flower spikes hum with bees and perfume the warm summer air. Late June is peak season, when the countryside turns into waves of purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, peaking around late June to July in Provence
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Big, cloud-like blooms burst from the shrubs in rounded mounds of petal-like sepals, brightening cottage gardens and shady corners as summer begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Gardens in Japan, the United Kingdom, and the eastern United States
plants.funFact: Soil chemistry can change the flower color. Acidic soil with available aluminum tends to produce blue blooms, while alkaline soil tends to produce pink ones.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: Star-shaped white blossoms with golden centers float on still, calm water among broad green pads. They open in the morning sun and close again by afternoon.
plants.location: Lakes and slow-moving ponds across Europe, from the British Isles to the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: The flower stalks can grow to match the depth of the water, so the blooms always float on the surface.
